title: The last p-th root is outside the preceding root field
statement: Let p be prime, k a field of characteristic p, and Omega a field extension of k [def-pc-field-extension]. For n >= 0 let a_0,...,a_n in k have linearly independent universal differentials over F_p [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Let alpha_0,...,alpha_n in Omega satisfy alpha_i^p = a_i. Then alpha_n is not in k(alpha_0,...,alpha_(n-1)), the smallest subfield containing k and the preceding roots. No algebraic-closure assumption, dimension formula or monomial basis is part of the statement.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07DZ (10.158.3), displayed Frobenius computation and differential contradiction; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07DZ

proof.text: Let L = k(alpha_0,...,alpha_(n-1)). Let R be the k-span in Omega of the finitely many monomials with exponents 0 <= e_i < p. It contains 1 and the generators since p > 1. Reducing each exponent modulo p, using alpha_i^p = a_i in k, proves that the product of two monomials lies in R. Bilinearity then shows R is a finite-dimensional k-subalgebra and a domain.

By the finite-dimensional-domain-is-field lemma, R is a field: injective multiplication by a nonzero element is surjective. Thus L is contained in R by minimality of field adjunction; R is contained in L because L contains every spanning monomial. Hence L = R. No independence or degree computation has been assumed.

If alpha_n lies in L, write it as sum_E lambda_E alpha^E using the preceding span description. Frobenius is additive and multiplicative in characteristic p, so a_n = sum_E lambda_E^p a^E. This equality holds in k because k -> Omega is injective.

Apply the universal derivation d:k -> Omega_(k/F_p). Leibniz gives d(lambda_E^p)=0 and d(a^E)=sum_(j:e_j>0) e_j a^(E-unit_j) d(a_j). Thus d(a_n) is a k-linear combination of d(a_j), j<n. Moving terms to one side produces a linear relation with coefficient 1 at n, contradicting independence. For n=0 it is simply d(a_0)=d(lambda^p)=0. This proves the stated nonmembership.

mathlib_searches.query: If differentials of a finite family in a characteristic p field are linearly independent then the last p-th root is not in the field generated by the previous roots
A p-th root of the last element of a differentially independent family is not in the field generated by p-th roots of earlier elements

theorem pth_root_not_mem_previous_adjoin
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharP k p]
    (Ω : Type v) [Field Ω] [Algebra k Ω]
    (n : ℕ) (a : Fin (n + 1) → k)
    (hind : LinearIndependent k
      (fun i : Fin (n + 1) ↦ KaehlerDifferential.D (ZMod p) k (a i)))
    (α : Fin (n + 1) → Ω)
    (hα : ∀ i : Fin (n + 1), α i ^ p = algebraMap k Ω (a i)) :
    α (Fin.last n) ∉ adjoin k (Set.range (fun i : Fin n ↦ α i.castSucc))
